subject: Follow-up: Ephemeral cache sweep and evidence summary — no customer data exposure
messages:
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: ops@acme-payments.com
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-20T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Incident 2027-05-20 — ephemeral cache anomaly

Hi Sam,

Thanks for the alert and for sharing the traces. We kicked off an immediate cache sweep and a full hash reconciliation against the KV store backing your dedicated pool. Dylan and Evelyn are pulling forensic extracts now — I wanted to let you know our scope and expected timeline:

- Scope: ephemeral in-memory KV cache and the disk-backed prefix cache for the tenant pool serving Acme Payments.
- Evidence collected: cache dumps (anonymized), server-side request logs (token-level masked), and signed hash manifests for artifacts.
- ETA: preliminary findings within 24 hours, full artifacts and signed manifest within 48 hours.

We will not publish raw logs containing any customer PII. For traceability we will provide SHA256 manifests and a short summary showing the ranges we inspected.

If you want a call to walk through the artifacts, I can schedule one with Dylan (forensics lead) and Evelyn (security).

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142


From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ops@acme-payments.com
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-20T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Incident 2027-05-20 — ephemeral cache anomaly

Hi all,

Quick status update from the forensics side: we've pulled the KV cache snapshots for the time window Sam flagged (2027-05-19 22:00 - 2027-05-20 02:00 UTC) across all pods in the dedicated pool. Steps taken:

1) Created immutable snapshots and stored them to an isolated forensic bucket (read-only).
2) Generated SHA256 for each artifact and recorded a manifest (attached).
3) Ran token-pattern heuristics and identifier scanning (names, email regexes, cc numbers) against the anonymized dataset.

Preliminary result: no matches to customer-identifiable patterns found in the ephemeral caches. We still need to run cross-checks against request logs for any unusual outbound connections, but so far there is no sign of data residency loss.

Attaching: sweep_report_20270522.csv, hash_manifest_20270522.txt.

Next actions: finish log-level egress scan and provide a signed summary by end of day tomorrow.

- Dylan (forensics)
Dylan Brooks
Staff Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference


From: ops@acme-payments.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: security@acme-payments.com
Date: 2027-05-21T07:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Incident 2027-05-20 — ephemeral cache anomaly

Kimberly/Dylan —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple of asks from our side before you finalize:

- Can you confirm the exact bucket path and provide the SHA256 manifest so our security team can independently verify the artifact integrity?
- Please include the query ids (redacted) used to pull the cache snapshots so we can map back to our internal telemetry.
- Any evidence of unexpected outbound requests from the inference pods to external endpoints during the window?

We'd prefer a short readout call once you have the signed summary.

Regards,
Sam Ortiz
SRE, Acme Payments
ops@acme-payments.com


From: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
To: ops@acme-payments.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-21T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Ephemeral cache sweep — final evidence summary and signed manifest

Sam, Kimberly —

Attached is the final sweep summary and the signed manifest. Key points:

- Artifacts inspected: 18 KV snapshot files (pod-range 3a-3f), 3 prefix-cache archives, and the request log slices covering the time window.
- Integrity: All artifacts stored in gs://redwood-forensics/ACME/INC-5421/ are accompanied by SHA256 entries in hash_manifest_20270522.txt and signed by our internal forensics key (PEM signature attached).
- Findings: No PII or customer-identifiable patterns were present in any ephemeral cache snapshots. The identifier-scanning heuristics and sample regex checks returned zero hits.
- Egress: Network flows show no outbound connections to unknown/third-party endpoints from the affected pods during the window. A single connection to telemetry.redwood-cdn.net is expected (heartbeat metrics) and contains only aggregated telemetry — no request payloads.

Attached artifacts: sweep_report_20270522.csv, hash_manifest_20270522.txt, kv-sample-archive.tar.gz (anonymized sample).

For chain-of-custody: each artifact has a timestamped manifest entry and was placed in an isolated bucket with ACLs restricted to the incident response team. We can provide the signed manifest for your internal verification.

If you want the raw manifests verified together on a short call I can join tomorrow morning PST.

— Evelyn Hart
Security Response Lead, Redwood Inference
evelyn_hart@redwood.com


From: ops@acme-payments.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, security@acme-payments.com
Date: 2027-05-22T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ephemeral cache sweep — final evidence summary and signed manifest

Evelyn/Kimberly —

Thanks for the thorough write-up. A few clarifying items from our security team:

1) Can you include the artifact SHA256 manifest lines in-line in the report (not only as attachments)? We need them for automated verification.
2) Please confirm whether the anonymization process removed any timestamps or identifiers that we will need to reconcile with our telemetry. We want a reproducible mapping between your artifact names and our request ids.

If both are possible, we are comfortable moving this to closure and marking ACME incident INC-5421 as mitigated.

Best,
Sam Ortiz
SRE, Acme Payments


From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: ops@acme-payments.com
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com, security@acme-payments.com
Date: 2027-05-22T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Closure: result of cache sweep and artifact verification (INC-5421)

Sam —

Appreciate the review and the clear next steps. To close the loop:

- Inline manifest excerpt (first three lines):
  - 3a_snapshot_20270520_2205.tar.gz  e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855
  - 3b_snapshot_20270520_2210.tar.gz  9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08
  - prefix_cache_20270520_2230.tar.gz  a54d88e06612d820bc3be72877c74f257b561b19e6d6e9f5b5b1f2a6e6d7f8c1

- Anonymization note: timestamps in the artifacts are preserved; request ids were hashed with a reversible mapping key that we can share via a secure key transfer (DocuSign-style signature exchange or your KMS). We did not strip timestamps; only direct PII patterns (emails, names, cc numbers) were redacted or replaced with tokens.

- Verification options: you can pull the artifacts from gs://redwood-forensics/ACME/INC-5421/ and verify the SHA256 lines against the included manifest. Evelyn is available for a live verification at 10:00 AM PST tomorrow if you want a walkthrough.

Conclusion (short): After artifact-level hash reconciliation, identifier scanning, and an egress flow check, we found no evidence of customer data exposure or exfiltration. We consider the incident mitigated for Acme Payments.

If you'd like a signed attestation letter (PDF) for your compliance records, we can send that via your procurement contact.

Thanks again for the partnership on this.

Kimberly Park
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
